description.ncbi_summary: The protein encoded by this gene functions as a regulator of G protein-coupled receptor signaling in phototransduction. Studies in bovine and mouse show that this gene is expressed only in the retina, and is localized in the rod outer segment membranes. This protein is associated with a heterotetrameric complex, specifically interacting with the regulator of G-protein signaling 9, and appears to function as the membrane anchor for the other largely soluble interacting partners. Mutations in this gene are associated with prolonged electroretinal response suppression (PERRS), also known as bradyopsia. [provided by RefSeq, Mar 2010].

uniprot_function.text: Membrane anchor protein of the photoreceptor RGS9-1-Gbeta5L complex (By similarity). Targets the complex to photoreceptor outer segment membranes and is required for its stability and full functional activity (PubMed:14702087). Promotes phototransduction recovery by enabling efficient RGS9-1-mediated deactivation of transducin signaling (PubMed:14702087).
